situation.roe_position: The return on equity is far above normal because of an exceptional underwriting stretch. The Property-Liability combined ratio fell to 85.1 in nine months of 2026, and 2025 was 85.2, from 104.5 in 2023. Large prior-year reserve releases helped, and so did higher net investment income. 2025 also included disposition gains. Equity was small after the 2022-23 losses, which inflates the ratio. Part of the margin will fade as releases shrink, catastrophe losses revert to the ten-year average and auto pricing softens. Equity has also grown, so the ratio mechanically falls.
situation.why: 2025 return of 0.5229 on a depressed opening equity base included about $1.1 billion of after-tax disposition gains and $1.8 billion of reserve releases, so it is not repeatable. The company is returning capital well above its dividend ($2,904 million of buybacks in nine months of 2026), so regulatory capital is not binding growth now. Subsidiary dividend limits and rating-agency capital metrics are a latent constraint, but the evidence shows no sign they bind.

situation.roe_position: ROE is far above any normal level. It rests on a very strong underwriting cycle: the Property-Liability combined ratio fell from 104.5 in 2023 to 85.2 in 2025 and 85.1 over nine months of 2026, aided by large prior-year reserve releases and higher net investment income. The ROE is also measured on an opening equity base that was small after the 2022-23 losses. Over the years in the record the ROE ranged from -6% to +52%.
situation.why: The 2025 ROE of 52% reflects peak underwriting margins, about $1.8bn of reserve releases and about $1.1bn of disposal gains, so it is not a base to extrapolate. Capital is not binding: Allstate is returning most earnings through buybacks, and book equity growth is a choice about payout, not a regulatory limit. The holding company still depends on dividends from regulated subsidiaries, and some states limit insurer profits, so ROE should fade toward the mid-teens as pricing competition, reserve releases and catastrophe normalization take effect.
